validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and correctly classified. This is one of five GEM segment rows (P3584-P3588) for WBI Energy Transmission, Inc.'s FERC-certificated North Bakken Expansion Project (Docket CP20-52), filed 2020-02-14, amended 2020-07-28, approved via a FERC Environmental Assessment issued 2021-10-23 (cms.ferc.gov, also archived on Wayback). FERC's own facility table (Table A-2 of the EA) lists 'Tioga Compressor Lateral, Williams County, MP 0.0-0.5, 0.5 mi' as a distinct new-pipeline facility, separate from the Tioga-Elkhorn Creek main (62.8 mi/24 in = P3584), Line Section 25 Loop (20.3 mi/12 in = P3585), Line Section 30 Loop (9.6 mi/12 in = P3586), and Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border (0.3 mi/24 in = P3588). Independently corroborated by WBI Energy's own project page (current, live), the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook (Docket CP20-52, Completed 2022-01-26), the Minot Daily News (construction start, project cost) article, and an Oil & Gas Journal piece on the Hess Tioga Gas Plant that this lateral effectively serves. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other roster row -- it is a genuine, separately-mileposted facility within the same certificated project as its four siblings; the interconnect relationship (this lateral runs from the Tioga Plant Receipt Station to new facilities at the Tioga Compressor Station, which also anchors the Line Section 30 Loop and the Tioga-Elkhorn Creek main) is expected project topology, not evidence of double-counting. CAVEAT (spec): GEM's Capacity field on ALL FIVE of these segment rows reads the identical 250.00 MMcf/d -- that is the PROJECT's total incremental design capacity (confirmed by the FERC EA's amended-application language, WBI Energy's own 'Key Stats' page, and the Minot Daily News), not a throughput figure intrinsic to this specific 0.5-mile compressor lateral, which (being a short interconnecting pipe between a receipt station and the compressor station, not an independent transportation path) has no separately reported capacity of its own. The EIA workbook records a close but distinct project total of 245 MMcf/d (vs. 250 in the other three sources) -- a minor, immaterial discrepancy, noted for completeness rather than treated as a conflict. I have NOT added a ref that would imply this project-total figure specifically validates the segment row's Capacity cell (see the Capacity fill below, staged UNRESOLVED for exactly this reason) -- flagging the aggregate-on-segment pattern here rather than silently treating a system source as segment-level support. Opened and read to exhaustion: FERC EA (CP20-52, 29MB PDF, full text extracted and searched), WBI Energy project page, Minot Daily News article, EIA Historical Projects workbook, Oil & Gas Journal Hess Tioga Gas Plant article; attempted but blocked/rate-limited: NS Energy Business page (403 to scripted UA), Williston Herald article (dead, 404), web.archive.org lookups for both (429 rate limit persisted across retries, likely from concurrent fan-out load on archive.org -- not pursued further given four other working independent sources already in hand).

validity.recommendation: clarify or flag that Capacity=250 MMcf/d on this row is the PROJECT's system-wide incremental design capacity (also stated identically on P3584/P3585/P3586/P3588), not a value measured for this 0.5-mile lateral specifically; no source states a capacity intrinsic to this short interconnecting segment
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity=250.00 MMcf/d is stated for the North Bakken Expansion PROJECT as a whole in three independent sources (FERC EA's amended-application language: 'incremental firm transportation design capacity of 250,000 [sic, read as 250] MMcf/d'; WBI Energy's own project page 'Key Stats': 'Providing up to 250 million cubic feet per day'; Minot Daily News, quoting Sen. Hoeven: 'an additional 250 million cubic feet per day of natural gas takeaway capacity'), and a close variant (245 MMcf/d) in the EIA historical-projects workbook. None of the four sources assigns a capacity figure to the Tioga Compressor Lateral specifically -- the lateral is a short (0.5 mi) interconnecting pipe between the Tioga Plant Receipt Station and new compressor-station facilities, not an independent transportation path with its own throughput rating. The same 250 MMcf/d value is recorded identically on all five North Bakken Expansion segment rows in the roster (P3584/P3585/P3586/P3587/P3588), which is the signature of a project total restated on every segment rather than five independently measured segment capacities. This is a spec-accuracy caveat, not an existence or classification problem -- the underlying pipe is real and correctly described everywhere else.

cross_row_leads.facts: Tioga-Elkhorn Creek pipeline: ~62.8 mi of new 24-in pipe, Williams (MP 0.0-25.3) then McKenzie County (MP 25.3-62.8), MAOP 1,480 psig, bi-directional; filed 2020-02-14, amended 2020-07-28, construction began July 2021, in service Feb 1 2022 (WBI Energy site) / EIA Completed 2022-01-26; project cost ~$260-260.5M; Capacity 250 (WBI/press/FERC) or 245 (EIA) MMcf/d is the PROJECT total, not specific to this segment.

Line Section 25 Loop: ~20.3 mi of new 12-in looping pipe across Williams (0.0-6.7), Mountrail (6.7-10.3), and Burke (10.3-20.3) Counties, between the Tioga Compressor Station and the proposed Norse Transfer Station, MAOP 1,098 psig, bi-directional, looping an existing 8-in line (MAOP 700 psig). Same project dates/costs/capacity caveats as P3584.

Line Section 30 Loop: ~9.6 mi of new 12-in looping pipe in Williams County, between the existing Nesson Valve Setting and the Tioga Compressor Station, MAOP 700 psig, bi-directional. Same project dates/costs/capacity caveats as P3584.

Elkhorn Creek-Northern Border pipeline: ~0.3 mi of new 24-in pipe in McKenzie County, between the proposed Elkhorn Creek Compressor Station and the new interconnect with Northern Border, MAOP 1,480 psig. Same project dates/costs/capacity caveats as P3584.

summary: P3587 (Tioga Compressor Lateral, North Bakken Expansion): confirmed (caveat) -- real, correctly classified, FERC-certificated (CP20-52) facility with no existence/duplicate/attribution problems; one spec concern (Capacity=250 MMcf/d is the project total, not this 0.5-mi lateral's own figure, contested but no substitute value proposed). 12 fills staged REFS_ADDED (Status, Fuel, Proposal, Construction, Start, Pressure, Length, Diameter, FuelSource, Location, Operator, Owner); Capacity and SegmentCost UNRESOLVED (no segment-specific source for either).
